items.title: Goal: ground-state energy of H₂ within 10⁻³
items.description: The system must estimate the lowest energy of the two-qubit H₂ Hamiltonian, accurate to 0.001 Hartree, compared with exact diagonalisation.

items.title: Fit the problem on 2 qubits
items.description: Use a reduced two-qubit encoding of H₂ so the circuit runs on any simulator and small hardware.

items.title: Choose a gradient-free optimiser
items.description: Estimating gradients on quantum hardware is expensive, so the classical side uses COBYLA, which only needs energy values.

items.title: Write the Hamiltonian as Pauli terms
items.description: Express H₂ as a weighted sum of Pauli strings (II, IZ, ZI, ZZ, XX) that an estimator can measure.

items.title: Ansatz: RY layers with one CX
items.description: A hardware-efficient ansatz: one layer of RY rotations, an entangling CX, then a second RY layer. Four parameters.

items.title: Interface: energy(params) → float
items.description: The single contract between both sides: the optimiser proposes parameters, the quantum side returns an energy.

items.title: Optimiser wrapper
items.description: minimize_energy(cost, x0) wraps scipy's COBYLA. It knows nothing about quantum computing.

items.title: VQE loop
items.description: Connect the estimator, the ansatz and the optimiser, and record the energy history.

items.title: Sanity check: Bell state
items.description: Run quantum/bell.py: the simulator must return only 00 and 11, roughly half each.

items.title: Compare with exact diagonalisation
items.description: The VQE energy must be within 10⁻³ of numpy's lowest eigenvalue.

items.title: Check the optimised state
items.description: Measure the optimised circuit and confirm the distribution concentrates on the expected basis state.

items.title: Results are repeatable
items.description: Seeds are fixed, so “Reproduce this run” in the History tab must give identical results.

items.title: Choose where the circuit runs
items.description: Today: QIDEA's local simulator. Later: real hardware behind the same backend.run() interface.

items.title: Package the project
items.description: Export the project as a zip with qidea.lock so anyone can run it with the same versions.

items.title: Keep runtimes up to date
items.description: When a new Qiskit version is available, run once with it, compare results, then update qidea.lock.
